newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market waits for hint on rates.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market waits for hint on rates.

text.p: A slight rise in Dutch call money on Monday was attributed to late effects of a tight allocation under last week's special advances pact.
"It's the first day there's some real trade in call since the allocation, and apparently, allocation wasn't that ample," one dealer said.
Last Friday, dealers had qualified the allocation as being broadly in line with the market's needs.
Call money was quoted between 2.81 and 2.93 percent bid, while dealers said trade was done around 2.87 percent.
The other money market rates all moved up one or two basis points since there were few sellers in the market, dealers said.

Volume in trade in DTCs was close to nil, one dealer said. Payment for DTCs purchased now has to be made in the third week of February, making them unattractive for many money market players, he said.
"It's hard to know now what your position will look like in three weeks' time," he said.
Activity was concentrated on overnight money and deposits up to three months, dealers said.
"As people are uncertain about the direction of the interest rates, they prefer to stay close to home, while they wait and see what'll happen," one dealer said.
The guilder was trading at 112.3313 per 100 marks.
